key_insight: Transient ion current (TIC/BACE) in perovskite solar cells is often limited by transport-layer capacitance, not by the perovskite’s true ionic density.
engineering_relevance: Accurate ionic parameter extraction requires accounting for transport-layer thickness, doping, and interfacial charge storage to avoid overestimating ion density by orders of magnitude.
method: Drift-diffusion simulations to compare TIC response against mobile-ion screening limits.
Systematic experiments varying C60 electron-transport-layer thickness in p-i-n devices and Spiro-OMeTAD hole-transport-layer doping in n-i-p devices.
Trend extrapolation and correction based on average ionic displacement to estimate absorber ionic conductivity, density, and mobility.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulation and experimental trends that match across architectures, showing TIC sensitivity changes primarily with transport-layer properties and that extrapolation can recover the absorber’s ionic conductivity.
watch_item: Interpreting TIC without correcting for transport-layer capacitance or trapped-carrier release can substantially inflate the inferred ionic signal.
paper_title: Overcoming Transport Layer Bottlenecks to Quantify Ionic Parameters from Transient Ion Current Measurements of Perovskite Solar Cells
